content.title: About
content.content: A wheat bun is a soft, slightly sweet roll made from wheat flour, commonly used as the base for sandwiches. Its airy crumb holds sauces and fillings well without becoming soggy too quickly.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Traditional wheat buns are made from simple ingredients: wheat flour, water, yeast, salt, and a touch of sugar.
In many countries buns are shaped either round or rectangular to fit packaging and sandwich assembly lines.
Buns are often lightly toasted before serving to add a crisp crust and prevent sogginess from sauces.
In the United States the “soft roll” variant is popular, containing more fat and sugar for extra tenderness.
Whole‑grain wheat buns can be made by incorporating whole‑grain flour, boosting fiber content.

items.title: Source of carbohydrates
items.content: Provides a quick source of energy through easily digestible carbs.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Wheat flour supplies thiamine, niacin, and folate, supporting metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Fiber content (in whole‑grain versions)
items.content: Whole‑grain buns are rich in dietary fiber, promoting healthy digestion.

items.title: Low fat
items.content: Traditional buns have minimal fat, fitting well into balanced diets.

items.title: Versatile pairing
items.content: Neutral flavor makes the bun compatible with a wide range of fillings, encouraging varied nutrition.

items.title: Wheat/gluten allergy
items.content: People with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity may experience adverse reactions to wheat buns.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: White wheat buns can cause rapid blood‑sugar spikes, which may be problematic for diabetics.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some buns contain added salt; those monitoring sodium intake should choose low‑salt options.

items.title: Preservatives and additives
items.content: Commercially produced buns may include flavor enhancers and preservatives that are not suitable for everyone.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Use wheat buns as the foundation for sandwiches, adding meat, fish, vegetables, cheese, and sauces. Lightly toast them for a crunchy crust or enjoy them cold in a classic deli sandwich. Mini buns work well for bite‑size snacks and appetizers.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep buns in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2‑3 days. For longer storage, freeze them in a zip‑top bag – they stay fresh for 2‑3 months. Reheat in an oven or toaster before use to restore softness.
